source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 124: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: compare per-GPU memory, communication topology, layer partitioning, batch and microbatch behavior, synchronization, latency target, and failure/reconfiguration costs.
corrected_answer: Scenario variant 124: Do not choose TP or PP without measurements. Assume a fixed checkpoint, precision, GPU count/type, usable memory in GiB, placement, interconnect, software versions, clock policy, request-length mix, load, concurrency, batching, and p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, TTFT, and TPOT targets in ms. Define throughput units, quality, error, and availability gates; label unknowns as assumptions. Pre-register: at a named load and fixed gates, the selected feasible configuration reduces held-out p99 latency by at least M ms or M% versus the best feasible alternative, with M fixed before evaluation. Enumerate TP degrees and PP layer partitions. Measure shard memory, collective bytes/time, topology, synchronization and stragglers for TP; stage balance, activation memory, transfer, microbatch count, bubbles, and queueing for PP. Use randomized repeated paired trials on isolated hardware, identical traces, fixed confounders, separate tuning and held-out data, stratified lengths/load, and confidence intervals. Record latency, throughput, memory, utilization, communication, bubbles, queueing, quality, errors, and recovery with units. Accept only configurations passing all gates; test authorized isolated failure handling and rollback to the last known-good configuration. If no option passes, report inconclusive rather than speculate.
risks: No platform measurements or thresholds are supplied; recommendation is conditional.
Topology, microbatching, request mix, thermal state, and queueing may confound latency.
Failure testing can disrupt service unless isolated and authorized.
evidence_required: Hardware/topology/software inventory and usable memory in GiB.
Repeated paired train/held-out results with latency, throughput, communication, bubbles, queueing, quality, errors, and recovery in stated units.
